results.response:
**Source note:** Live Google data is unavailable this turn — our Google API quota is exhausted platform-wide and doesn't reset until 2026-07-29 08:03 UTC. The figures below come from the captured historical store (the dashboard's own source), which is unaffected. Both quarters are fully covered by capture (Google capture floor 2020-01-27), so these are complete, settled totals.

## Google Ads — Q4 2024 vs Q4 2023

| Metric | Q4 2024 | Q4 2023 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | $127,677.28 | $111,683.47 | **+$15,993.81 (+14.3%)** |
| Impressions | 92,845 | 84,185 | +10.3% |
| Clicks | 5,010 | 2,721 | +84.1% |
| CTR | 5.40% | 3.23% | +2.17 pts |
| CPC | $25.48 | $41.05 | −37.9% |
| Conversions | 683 | 155 | +340.6% |
| CPA | $186.94 | $720.54 | **−74.1%** |

### Read

**You spent 14% more and got 4.4x the leads.** The spend increase is modest and roughly tracks impression growth (+10%), so this isn't a budget-driven story — it's an efficiency story. The engine of it sits in the click layer: impressions only grew 10% but clicks grew 84%, so CTR went from 3.23% to 5.40%. That's a relevance/creative/query-match improvement, not more reach.

**CPC fell from $41.05 to $25.48.** For residential remodeling in North Jersey those are both punishing numbers, but a 38% reduction on effectively flat auction volume points to better Quality Score or a mix shift away from the most expensive head terms.

**CPA is the headline: $720.54 → $186.94.** Conversion rate on clicks went from 5.7% to 13.6%, so roughly half the CPA improvement came from cheaper clicks and half from clicks that actually converted — landing page and offer alignment, not just auction dynamics.

### Caveats before you take the CPA win to the client

- **Conversion counting is the thing to verify.** A 341% conversion jump against a 84% click jump is large enough that it's worth confirming no conversion actions were added, re-scoped, or switched to enhanced/modeled conversions between Q4 2023 and Q4 2024. If the counting basis changed, part of that CPA drop is measurement, not performance.
- **Ignore ROAS here.** The store reports conversionValue of $576 (2024) and $155 (2023) — those are placeholder/proxy values, not real revenue, and there's no store or GA revenue source attached to this account. For an offline-sales and lead client, CPA and lead volume are the right scorecard; any ROAS figure on this account is meaningless.
- **This is Google only.** Meta, Shopify and WooCommerce aren't connected for this client, so there's no cross-channel view to pair against it.

If you want, I can break Q4 2024 down by campaign or pull the search term mix for both quarters to isolate where the CTR and CPC improvement actually came from.
